Treatise is defined as a formal systematic written discourse, a specific kind of document. Specific->general holds.

Comparator is a circuit component / building block, not a measurement instrument in the ordinary sense. Instruments are user-facing measurement devices with readouts; comparator is an internal electronic element used within instruments and processors. The nearest kind is electronic circuit or comparator circuit, not instrument. The kind-of claim is a leap past nearer kinds, violating Law 11e.

A clipper is a specific hard-limiting amplitude processor that truncates peaks at a threshold, which is a form of amplitude limiting. In audio engineering practice, clipping is treated as an extreme case of limiting, with infinite ratio. The kind-of relationship holds with limiter as the nearest general kind.

Measurement's accepted definition carves the act of comparing a quantity to a standard unit. Gain is a ratio quantity, not the act of measuring. The note pins gain as a type of measurement but the target's definition carves measurement as an act. Law 9a: a thing is not an instance of the act that measures it; gain is the object of measurement, not an instance of measurement itself. The peers' reasoning is correct.

A treatise is defined as a formal systematic written discourse on a subject. The accepted definition explicitly carves it as a discourse genre. The kind-of relationship to discourse is direct and the nearest general kind on the communicative axis.

Saturation's accepted definition carves a general capacity-boundary state across systems, media, and perceptual fields, not specifically audio distortion. The edge claims saturation is a kind of distortion, which misclassifies the general state as a specific audio effect. The pinned sense borrows audio usage not carved in the accepted definition. The challenge correctly identifies MISCLASSIFICATION.

Waveshaping is a nonlinear signal-processing method applying a static amplitude transfer function. Saturation is a general capacity-boundary state. A method is not a kind of a boundary state. The kind-of claim misclassifies and uses an audio-usage sense of saturation not carved in the accepted definition. Challenge correctly identifies MISCLASSIFICATION.

parallel-compression is a genuine audio technique with a well-carved definition: it blends compressed and uncompressed signals to preserve transients while increasing perceived loudness. This is a real, parameterized technique deserving to be in the record.

parallel-compression IS a specific kind of audio-effect. The note pins the right sense: an audio effect that intentionally alters a sound signal by blending compressed and dry versions. Specific→general to the nearest kind.
threshold IS a boundary in the accepted definition sense. The note correctly identifies that boundary includes THRESHOLD as a species, so this is not a ladder leap. Direction: specific→general.
tempo IS a measurement: it quantifies the speed of a beat cycle in BPM. A competent speaker in music would call tempo a type of measurement. Nearest general kind is measurement.
phase IS a measurement: it quantifies angular offset between two periodic waveforms, measured in degrees or radians. Nearest general kind is measurement.
amplitude IS a measurement: it quantifies the magnitude/strength of a signal. A competent speaker in physics or audio would call amplitude a type of measurement. Nearest general kind is measurement.
frequency IS a measurement: it quantifies cycles per unit time in Hertz. A competent speaker would call frequency a type of measurement. Nearest general kind is measurement.

impedance IS a property: it is the opposition to current flow in an electrical circuit. A competent speaker in electronics would call impedance a type of property — specifically an electrical property. Nearest general kind is property.
rubicon IS a boundary: a point of no return — a critical threshold. Both literal and figurative usage denote a boundary. Nearest kind is boundary.

headroom quantifies the difference between nominal and maximum operating level — a measurement quantity. A competent audio engineer would describe headroom as a measured value. Nearest general kind is measurement.

parallel-compression IS a specific kind of dynamic-range-compression technique: it applies compression to a copy of the signal and blends the compressed signal with the dry original. The sense matches the accepted definition — drc encompasses any technique that alters the dynamic range, and parallel compression does exactly that (just with a parallel dry/wet mix). Specific→general holds.

parallel-compression INSTANCE_OF audio-effect is a leap, not nearest kind. Audio-effect is a broad category — parallel compression is more specifically a dynamic-range-compression technique (see Seth's edge to drc). Unless drc INSTANCE_OF audio-effect exists, audio-effect is too far up the ladder. File against the nearest kind, not a parent of the nearest kind.

Threshold IS a specific kind of boundary: its accepted definition states it is a defined point of crossing mediating between two states, converting separation into selective passage. A threshold is exactly a boundary that marks a crossing point. Specific→general holds.

parallel-compression is a well-defined human-made audio technique. Scope correctly identifies it as an audio dynamics technique blending compressed and uncompressed signals. Law 3b referent is THING (a method/practice). Law 1 scope is clear.

Comparator DEPENDS_ON threshold: removal test holds — a comparator's binary output is defined at the crossing point where its inputs reverse, and that transition point IS the threshold. Without a threshold (a defined crossing point between states) there is no point at which the comparator's output flips, so its comparison function ceases to operate. This is mechanism→defining-parameter, not purpose; consistent with the accepted limiting→threshold. Direction from→to (comparator needs threshold) is correct.

Preamp DEPENDS_ON gain: a preamp is a gain stage — its defining operating quantity is the ratio of output to input amplitude. Remove the concept of gain and a preamp has no measurable function: it would still pass current, but 'preamplifying a weak signal' is precisely providing gain, so the device ceases to OPERATE as a preamp. This is mechanism→defining-quantity (like screwdriver→screw, limiting→threshold), and the note's sense (ratio of output to input amplitude) matches the accepted gain entry. Direction correct.

Comparator DEPENDS_ON signal: clean functional-input dependency. A comparator compares two input signals; remove the concept of signal (an entity carrying information/energy through a medium) and the comparator has nothing to compare — no inputs, no comparison, no output meaning. The note pins the signal sense correctly and the removal test is present-tense necessity, not chronology. Direction from→to (comparator needs signal) is correct.

Gain DEPENDS_ON amplification fails the removal test. Gain is the filed quantity — the ratio of output to input amplitude — and it is defined for ANY system with an input and output, including attenuators (gain < 1), passive voltage dividers, and filters, none of which perform amplification. Remove the process of amplification and the quantity of gain still operates fully; an attenuator's gain of 0.5 exists with zero amplification. The note's premise that 'gain is precisely the quantitative measure of amplification' misreads the quantity: gain measures a ratio, not a process. If any edge is real here it runs the other way (amplification characterized by its gain), but that is not what is filed. STRIKE.

Saturation DEPENDS_ON gain fails the removal test. The accepted saturation definition is the point at which a system, medium, or perceptual field reaches MAXIMUM CAPACITY — additional input yields no further effect. Its parameters are capacity and input, not gain: an ADC saturating at full scale, a tape head overdriven into flux limit, or a perceptual field reaching saturation all occur with no gain stage at all. 'Driving gain beyond the design limit' (the filer's note) is one way to INDUCE saturation, not its defining mechanism — removing the concept of gain leaves saturation fully operational. The real dependency, if any, runs to capacity/headroom, not gain. STRIKE.

Compression DEPENDS_ON gain: Law 11d sense mismatch plus failed removal test. The accepted compression entry is 'the engineered practice of representing information using fewer resources than its original form while preserving a defined subset of its content' — parameters are an input stream and a mapping algorithm/encoding. Its persistence mechanism is algorithmic, not gain-based; remove gain and data compression operates untouched. The filer pinned an audio-dynamics sense ('reducing dynamic range') that is NOT the sense of this entry — that mechanism belongs to dynamic-range-compression, whose accepted definition is precisely the one operating by variable gain above a threshold. The correct edge (dynamic-range-compression DEPENDS_ON gain) is not what is filed. STRIKE.

Pinned sense holds: the accepted gain definition makes both operands signals (ratio of output signal magnitude to input signal magnitude). Removal test at the object level: with no signals there are no operands, and a ratio of nothing is nothing — gain stops operating. Signal is neither what gain IS (gain is a quantitative ratio, not a signal — identity would be 8c territory) nor what gain is for (no teleology here). This is the Law 11 corrective shape: measurement uses number → the court's correct edge was DEPENDS_ON; gain uses signal the same way. Not a meta-level 'gain as a concept needs language' claim (8b): the collapse is of gain's own working.

Law 9 test: is parallel-compression a specific kind of dynamic-range-compression? Yes — it applies compression to a copy of the signal and blends the compressed signal with the dry original; a competent audio engineer calls it a kind of (dynamic) compression. Nearest-rung check (Law 11e): the accepted ladder runs dynamic-range-compression INSTANCE_OF compression, so DRC is the direct parent and 'compression' the grandparent rung — this is the nearest kind, not a derivable leap (the only other path would run through this very pending edge). audio-effect is a sibling rung, not an ancestor, so the parallel Dakk edge does not subsume or conflict with this one. Pinned sense (a DRC technique, not a general effect) is exactly what the edge claims.

Removal test at the object level: a comparator's entire operation is detecting a crossing of a defined point — its output is the binary state of which side of the crossing the input sits on ('whether one exceeds the other' pins the other input as the reference threshold). Remove the concept of a threshold (defined crossing point between states) and the comparator has nothing to detect — its working collapses, not merely its sayability (8b passes). Not identity (8c): a comparator is a circuit, not a point — threshold is a functional principle its operation is defined by, not what it IS; same shape as the upheld compressor→threshold principle. Not teleology (8d): the comparator is not built for the sake of thresholds. The pinned sense is the detector sense, and it holds.

The note's own argument is teleological — 'its sole purpose is to provide gain to a weak signal' — and purpose is not dependency (Law 8c); where the note says 'X exists to serve Y' the arrow is SERVES at best, not DEPENDS_ON. Deeper: a preamp IS a gain stage — gain is its identity, not an external requirement, and 8c says a thing does not depend on what it is. The removal test fails at the operating level (8b): remove the concept of gain and the preamp's circuit still amplifies — transistor physics does not require the ratio that describes it; only the sayability of 'providing gain' is lost. Contrast the upheld gain→signal, where signals are the ratio's actual operands and collapse is of gain's own working. The preamp's real dependencies run to amplifier/amplification; the right edges are preamp INSTANCE_OF amplifier (nearest kind) or a dependency on the amplification process, not the measure of it.

Law 11d: the target's accepted definition carves amplification as the RHETORICAL technique — 'a rhetorical technique that strengthens a point by elaborating on it through varied expression, repetition with intensification' (auxesis). The note pins a different sense ('the process of increasing signal amplitude') that the target's accepted definition does not carve, and gain plainly does not depend on the rhetorical technique of elaborating a claim. A note pinning a sense the target does not hold argues a different question (11d), and where the disagreement is about which sense the entry should carry, the defect is in the definition — the move is a Law 30 REPLACE contest against the amplification definition, not this edge. Same failure shape as the earlier overdrive/compressor→amplification strikes. (The physics sense is live in the web — resonance INSTANCE_OF amplification and the SERVES-communication edge both lean on it — so the definition deserves a contest to carve it, but that does not make this edge true as filed.)

Law 8b removal test fails at the object level. The note pins the audio sense (soft clipping when signal exceeds a circuit's capacity) — a sense the web has accepted under saturation via its INSTANCE_OF rungs — but even on that pinning, gain is not what saturation operates by. Gain is the input/output RATIO: a description of the linear region and its departure. Remove the concept of gain and nothing stops saturating — the tape head still hits its flux ceiling, the diode still clips, the tank still fills, the market still saturates. The mechanism is the capacity CEILING and the input exceeding it; the ratio is a bookkeeping description of where the transfer function departs from linearity. 'Saturation IS the result of excessive gain' is constitutive assertion without a removal consequence (8b: constitutive ≠ dependency), and it misattributes the mechanism: you drive the INPUT past the limit, you do not 'drive gain' — gain is what gets reported as falling. The edge names a description of the state, not an operand of it.

Functional-operand necessity. A comparator (per its pending definition) is a circuit that compares two input signals and produces an output indicating their relationship — its operand IS signal: without signal there are no inputs and nothing to compare, the removal test passes at the object level. Same pattern as gain→signal: signal is what the comparator operates on, not a description of it. Direction dependent→operand is correct.

Measure-vs-process failure, same shape as preamp→gain. The accepted gain definition carves gain as a MEASURE — 'the ratio of an output signal magnitude to its corresponding input signal magnitude.' Compression's mechanism is threshold detection plus variable attenuation: remove the concept of gain and the sidechain still detects, the attenuator still attenuates, and dynamic range is still reduced. The note's 'lever' is the physical variable-gain stage, not the ratio concept — it conflates a physical stage with its bookkeeping description (8b: the claimed removal does not stop operation). Compression's real dependencies point at threshold and the attenuation process, not at the measure that reports it.

Parallel compression deliberately alters a sound signal for mix purposes — blending a compressed path with the dry signal to change dynamics (preserve transients, raise perceived loudness) — and is a specific kind of audio effect. Nearest kind is audio-effect: the web has no dynamics-processor rung, the same rung de-esser→audio-effect used when it was accepted. Specific→general per Law 9; a kind-of claim, not a ladder leap.

The target's accepted definition carves measurement as an ACT — 'the act of comparing a quantity to a standard unit.' Gain is not an act: its accepted definition carves it as 'the measure of amplification factor — the ratio of output magnitude to input magnitude', i.e. a quantity/parameter. The note's own argument proves the point — 'it quantifies the ratio' — the thing that quantifies a ratio is a value; the act that determines it is the measurement. gain is the OBJECT of a measurement (you measure gain), not an instance of measurement itself. Law 9a: a thing is not an instance of its own act/property; the true relation is that gain is what a measurement determines.

Genuine human-made construct (Laws 1-3): the mixing technique of running a parallel compression path and blending it with the dry signal to preserve transients while raising perceived loudness. Made-side, built to persist through recording-engineering practice, mixing manuals, and plugin implementations. The scope is a coherent, specific claim — not boilerplate or self-reference.

Parallel compression is a specific, named technique WITHIN dynamic range compression: it compresses a parallel copy of the signal and blends that compressed copy with the dry original (the 'glue'/'New York' practice). Direction is specific->general, and dynamic-range-compression is the nearest general kind a competent audio engineer would call it 'a kind of'. Clean Law 9 INSTANCE_OF; no leap, no sense-confusion. ADVANCE.

Removal test fails. Gain is the ratio of output to input magnitude and spans values on BOTH sides of unity: gain>1 amplifies, gain<1 attenuates. Remove the concept of amplification and gain still operates fully as the quantity describing attenuation, unity-gain, or level change. Amplification is a special case (gain>1) OF gain, not an operand gain needs to function. Law 8c: identity/specialization is not dependency. STRIKE.

The note argues purpose, not dependency: 'its sole purpose is to provide gain to a weak signal' is a Law 8c purpose-argument, which routes to SERVES, never DEPENDS_ON. The removal test independently fails: a preamp is a physical amplifier that raises a weak signal's level; remove the abstract concept of gain and the preamp still boosts — gain merely quantifies what it does. Law 8b: X keeps operating, it only loses a name/description. STRIKE.

The note says saturation is 'achieved by driving gain beyond the design limit', but that misstates the mechanism: saturation occurs when a signal exceeds a system's capacity at its FIXED operating point — the gain does not change, the input overshoots the valid range (overdrive a unity-gain stage and it still clips). Remove the concept of gain and saturation still occurs whenever level exceeds capacity. Removal test fails; the true operand is signal level against capacity, not gain. STRIKE.

Gain is, by its accepted definition, the ratio of an OUTPUT signal's magnitude to its INPUT signal's magnitude — both operands ARE signals. This is operand-necessity, not a measure-of: remove the concept of signal and gain has no operands to form a ratio of, so it ceases to operate. Contrast with the ->gain edges I struck (gain is the measure, not the operand). Clean Law 8 removal test on the pinned sense. ADVANCE.

A comparator is a circuit whose inputs are two electrical signals; its entire operation is comparing those signals. Remove the concept of signal and there is nothing for it to compare — it ceases to operate. Operand-necessity, Law 8 present-tense removal test satisfied on the pinned sense (electronic signal comparator). Consistent with gain->signal. ADVANCE.

Law 8b test: remove the concept of gain — does compression stop OPERATING, or does it merely stop being SAYABLE? A compressor keeps operating: it detects level above threshold and reduces the output level accordingly. 'Gain reduction' is the standard NAME for that level-modulation, not a separate operating ingredient. The note never shows the mechanism collapsing without the gain concept; it only restates that the mechanism is called gain reduction. Consistent with my strikes of preamp->gain and saturation->gain: gain is the measure, not the operand. STRIKE.

The note overstates the case: a comparator's essential function is COMPARING two inputs, and thresholding (one input fixed as a reference) is a common USE of comparison, not a requirement — a differential comparator compares two varying signals with no fixed threshold at all. Remove the concept of threshold and the comparator still operates, comparing whatever two signals it is given. Law 8 removal test fails; the note's 'entire function is to compare against a threshold' is false of the general construct. STRIKE.

Law 9a test: would a competent speaker call gain 'a kind of measurement'? No — they call it a parameter, a ratio, or a setting, and they say 'gain is MEASURED in dB', which positions gain as the OBJECT of measurement, not a measurement itself. A measurement is the act/process (or its result) of determining a quantity; gain is the quantity. A thing is not an instance of the process that measures it (cf. the established measurement->number correction: measurement USES number). The nearest kind for gain is a ratio/quantity, not measurement. STRIKE.

Gain is defined as the quantitative measure of amplification — ratio of output to input magnitude. Remove the concept of amplification and gain loses its referent: there is no operation to measure. The removal test passes; gain ceases to operate without amplification as the thing being measured. This is object-level dependency, not meta-level sayability.

A comparator's entire operational function is to compare an input signal against a threshold. Remove the concept of signal and the comparator has no operand to process; it ceases to operate. This is object-level functional necessity, not chronology or purpose.

Comparator's function is to compare a signal against a defined crossing point. Remove threshold and the comparator has nothing to compare against; it ceases to operate. Operational removal test passes.

Parallel-compression is a specific technique within dynamic-range-compression: it applies compression to a copy and blends with dry signal. This is the nearest kind; a competent speaker would call it a kind of dynamic-range-compression. INSTANCE_OF arrow is specific→general.

Gain's accepted definition is the ratio of output signal magnitude to input signal magnitude. Both operands are signals. Remove the concept of signal and gain has no magnitudes to relate; the ratio becomes undefined. Present-tense removal test passes: gain ceases to operate as a parameter without signals.

Compression in audio operates by reducing gain — gain reduction is its core mechanism. Remove the concept of gain and compression ceases to operate because there is no lever to act on. Operational removal test passes.

Preamp's purpose is to provide gain, but purpose is not dependency. Law 8c: identity is not dependency, purpose is not dependency. A preamp operates as an amplifier; gain is a parameter it exhibits, not an operational prerequisite. Remove the concept of gain and the preamp still operates as an amplifier — it still increases signal amplitude, gain is just the measure of that. The note confuses purpose with operational necessity.

Entry scope correctly carves a human-made audio dynamics technique with a clear persistence mechanism through DSP implementations and engineering practice. Name is lowercase noun, referent THING appropriate. Definition is pending but entry itself is coherent and within audio signal processing domain.

Definition carves upward expansion as a human-made dynamic-range processing technique with parameters threshold, expansion ratio, attack/release, knee, and mechanism of persistence via DSP algorithms in plugins and hardware. Ends with Law 6 trailer. Coherent and appropriate.

Upward expansion is a specific audio dynamics technique that alters a sound signal, fitting the accepted audio-effect carve. Note pins sense correctly and nearest kind is audio-effect per Law 11e. Coherent kind-of claim.

Gain is defined as ratio of output signal magnitude to input signal magnitude; both operands are signals. Remove the concept of signal and gain loses its operational referents — ratio becomes undefined. Present-tense operational dependency per Law 8b, direction dependent→operand correct.

Compression in audio operates by reducing gain when signal exceeds threshold. Remove gain concept and compression mechanism vanishes — no gain reduction lever. Present-tense operational dependency, note pins sense correctly.

Reconsidering after peer reasoning. Accepted saturation definition carves a general capacity-boundary state: point at which a system/medium/perceptual field reaches maximum capacity, beyond which additional input yields no further effect. Parameters are capacity and input, not gain. Saturation occurs at fixed operating points when input exceeds capacity — ADC full scale, tape flux limit, perceptual saturation — with no gain stage required. Gain is the input/output ratio, a description of the linear region, not an operand of the capacity ceiling. Removing gain leaves saturation fully operational; the mechanism is capacity ceiling and input exceeding it, not gain. The edge misattributes mechanism and fails Law 8b removal test against the accepted carve. STRIKE.
Gain is the quantitative measure of amplification; remove amplification concept and gain loses operational meaning. Note pins sense correctly to audio amplification. Present-tense dependency holds.

Upward expansion operates by comparing signal level against a threshold and applying gain to signals below it. Remove the threshold concept and the technique loses its trigger mechanism — there is no operational reference for when to engage. The removal test passes: the technique stops functioning without a threshold parameter. The note correctly pinns the technical sense of threshold as a level reference.

Saturation is controlled harmonic distortion achieved by driving a circuit into nonlinearity. Gain is the amplification factor — a parameter, not a dependency. Saturation does not DEPEND_ON gain; rather, it is a phenomenon that OCCURS at certain gain levels. The removal test: remove the concept of gain, and saturation as a circuit behavior concept still makes sense (it's about the nonlinear transfer characteristic, not the amplification magnitude). This is like saying 'flooding DEPENDS_ON water-level' — the level is the medium/parameter, not a dependency. Saturation DEPENDS_ON nonlinear-transfer-characteristic or clipping-circuit, not gain.

Well-specified audio processing technique. Scope correctly identifies it as human-made (DSP implementations, engineering practice) and maps the mechanism (increasing gain below threshold to expand dynamic range). This is a distinct technique from dynamic-range-compression — it works on the low end rather than the high end. The map boundaries are clear.

Definition carves well: specifies the mechanism (increases gain below threshold), the effect (expands perceived dynamic range), and the parameters (threshold, ratio, makeup gain). Ends with proper trailer. Distinguishes upward expansion from compression by working on the low end. This is a proper technical carving.

Upward expansion is a specific kind of audio effect — a competent audio engineer would call it 'an audio effect.' The note pins the correct sense: it alters sound signal character by increasing gain below threshold. This is a proper INSTANCE_OF against nearest kind (audio-effect), not a leap.

The challenge claims the definition fails to carve because it only covers rhetorical amplification while the accepted edges lean on the physics sense. But the current definition correctly carves the rhetorical sense, and physics-sense edges should be under a physics entry or be reclassified. The challenger's replacement still only covers rhetorical amplification (it's the same as the current definition), so the REPLACE claim is self-defeating. The honest path: keep the rhetorical entry, reclassify physics-sense edges. STRIKE the challenge.
Ducking is a specific form of dynamic-range compression: one signal is attenuated when another exceeds a threshold. This is a genuine specific→general kind relationship.

De-esser uses sidechain architecture: the detection path splits off to detect sibilance, and that detection triggers gain reduction on the main path. Remove sidechain and the de-esser loses its core operating mechanism.
Sidechain is a specific kind of signal-processing technique: routing one signal to control the processing of another. This is a genuine specific→general INSTANCE_OF.
Upward expansion requires a threshold to determine when to increase gain for signals below that level. Remove the threshold and the technique has no trigger reference — it stops operating.
Upward expansion is a specific kind of audio effect: it alters a sound signal by increasing gain below a threshold, changing perceptual character. The note correctly pins this sense.

Upward expansion is a genuine human-made audio dynamics technique. Scope correctly describes what it does (increases gain below threshold) and its persistence through DSP implementations and engineering practice.

Definition correctly carves upward expansion: specifies parameters (threshold, expansion ratio, attack/release), states the persistence mechanism (DSP implementations, engineering practice), and includes the Law 6 trailer. The definition is precise and distinct.

The contest screen says 'definition fails to carve' on amplification. Amplification as a rhetorical technique IS well-defined: base claim + elaboration + repetition with intensification + cumulative detail. The existing definition carves the construct clearly — it's a map of a specific rhetorical practice. The contest's challenge definition should be the target.

Removal test fails against the accepted sense. Acquittal is carved as 'a judicial act declaring a defendant not guilty of the charged offense — a binary outcome produced by a formal adjudicative process.' Remove the concept of evidence and that act still operates: acquittals are routinely rendered where no evidence is evaluated at all (prosecution declination, dismissal, statute expiration, procedural defaults). Evidence is an input a fact-finder may weigh, not the mechanism by which the acquittal operates — and structurally the reverse holds: under burden-of-proof allocation, acquittal is the outcome that fires precisely when evidence is ABSENT or insufficient. The note pins 'a verdict based on evaluation of evidence,' which carves one mode (trial acquittals), not the concept. The adjudicative process that actually produces the verdict is already captured by the accepted acquittal DEPENDS_ON law. STRIKE.

The which-came-first test needs a SPECIFIC historical channel through which the older construct fed the younger. The independent history of the due-process doctrine runs through concrete legal institutions: Magna Carta's 'law of the land' clauses (1215), 14th-century English administrative usage of 'due process of law' (the technical legal sense of 'process'), and the common-law procedural guarantees that later entered the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments. That channel is LAW — already captured by the accepted due-process DEPENDS_ON law and due-process INSTANCE_OF procedure. The note's argument — 'the idea that proceedings must follow fair rules came before the specific doctrine, which is a part of [justice]' — is breadth/containment, not derivation: justice is the ambient evaluative frame against which every legal doctrine is measured, and attributing the doctrine's origin to it restates the definition (due process = law's fair-procedure portion) without naming a channel by which the justice-concept fed the doctrine. Broad-heritage edges to an ambient frame are mass, not structure. STRIKE.

Which-came-first holds from independent history: law as an enforceable rules framework (codes, courts, enforcement) predates formal acquittal doctrine by millennia — Roman absolutio, Anglo-Saxon and common-law adjudication — and the channel is specific, not ambient: the legal system's development of formal adjudicative practice is precisely what PRODUCED the verdict type. The binary guilty/not-guilty finding is a product of institutional adjudication; no acquittal concept exists outside a legal system that renders it. The note pins exactly this: 'legal systems produced the concept of formal verdicts including conviction and acquittal.' Complementary, not duplicative: the accepted acquittal INSTANCE_OF verdict records the kind, the accepted acquittal DEPENDS_ON law records present-tense operation, and this DERIVED_FROM records the historical direction in which the legal institution forged the verdict type. ADVANCE.

A competent audio engineer calls ducking a form of compression — specifically sidechain/external-key compression: variable gain applied to one signal (background) under the control of another (foreground), reducing the effective dynamic range of the mix. The pinned sense matches the accepted dynamic-range-compression definition (reducing the loud-quiet difference via variable gain); the control-signal SOURCE is a parameter of the technique, not a kind difference — and the routing aspect is already separately captured by the accepted ducking DEPENDS_ON sidechain. Nearest-kind check (11e): no sidechain-compression entry exists; compressor is a DEVICE class and a technique is not an instance of a device (competent-speaker test fails there — one says ducking is done WITH a compressor, not that it IS one); and dynamic-range-compression is not yet reachable from ducking (its only accepted rung is ducking -> audio-effect, and audio-effect has no INSTANCE_OF parent), so this is a first true connection, not a redundant leap. ADVANCE.

De-esser's core architecture is a sidechain detector path: one signal (sibilant band) controls gain on the main signal. Remove that sidechain mechanism and the de-esser literally stops operating — no control path means no attenuation trigger. This is a removal-test DEPENDS_ON, not just sayability.

Acquittal is a verdict based on evaluation of evidence — insufficient evidence, absence of proof. Remove the concept of evidence and acquittal cannot operate: there is no basis for the verdict. This is a genuine DEPENDS_ON, not a meta-level linguistic dependency.

Due-process as a legal doctrine historically derived from the broader concept of justice. The question is which existed first: justice (a concept of fairness in proceedings) predates due-process (a specific legal mechanism) by millennia. The DERIVED_FROM direction is correct.

Ducking is a specific kind of dynamic-range processing: it reduces the level of one signal when a second exceeds a threshold, thereby compressing the dynamic range between them. A competent audio engineer would call ducking a form of compression. This is nearest-kind INSTANCE_OF.

Sidechain is a specific kind of signal-processing technique: it processes signals by routing one signal to control the processing of another. A competent engineer would call sidechaining a form of signal processing. Nearest-kind INSTANCE_OF.

Upward expansion is a human-made audio dynamics technique that increases gain for signals below a threshold to expand dynamic range. The scope correctly describes both the mechanism (gain increase below threshold) and the purpose (expand dynamic range). This is a genuine human-made construct.

Law 11d: overlap-save's accepted definition is an FFT-based linear convolution algorithm using block processing. The claim that it DEPENDS_ON windowing is factually false — standard overlap-save applies NO window function. It takes overlapping input blocks, zero-pads to FFT length, does circular convolution, and discards aliased samples. The removal test fails: remove FFT and overlap-save doesn't work, but remove windowing and it still works identically. DEPENDS_ON requires structural necessity, not an optional optimization.

Amplifier is NOT a kind of audio-effect. An audio effect is a device or algorithm that deliberately modifies timbre, character, or spatial properties of a signal (reverb, delay, chorus, etc.). An amplifier merely increases amplitude — it is the signal chain fundamental power stage, not a modifier of character. INSTANCE_OF requires specific→general, but amplifier is the upstream stage, not a subclass of effect.

Law 11d: judged against limiting's accepted definition as a dynamics processor (reduces gain above threshold to clamp output and prevent overshoot). The claimed sense — hard limiting clips peaks producing distortion — conflates the thresholding action with distortion. Hard limiting IS a form of clipping, but clipping ≠ distortion generically; the edge INSTANCE_OF distortion misclassifies a dynamics-processing construct as a distortion subclass. Nearest kind is a dynamics processor, not distortion.

Law 11d: the entry's accepted definition carves limiting as a dynamics processor that reduces gain above a set threshold to CLAMP the output and PREVENT overload or distortion — its design purpose is the opposite of producing distortion. The note pins a 'hard limiting that clips signal peaks' sense, but that construct is already named in the graph as 'clipping' (hard clipping = abrupt truncation at the limit), so the pinned sense is a different construct than the entry's accepted carving. A limiter is not a specific kind of distortion: a competent audio speaker would call it a dynamics processor (a kind of compressor — infinite-ratio limiting), and distortion's accepted definition carves effects that ADD grit/warmth/aggression by driving circuits beyond their linear range. If the filer meant the clipping construct, the nearest rung is 'clipping', not 'distortion' — and the sense still wouldn't ride on 'limiting'. The claim as filed fails the kind test.

Law 11d, judged on the pinned sense ('amplifier as used in audio signal processing'): the entry's accepted definition carves an amplifier as increasing amplitude 'while attempting to preserve the original waveform's shape and information content' — transparency is its design purpose. The accepted audio-effect definition carves a technique or device that 'intentionally alters a sound signal to change its perceptual character.' An amplifier's intended modification is level only; it is defined by what it does NOT change. A competent audio speaker would not call an amplifier 'a kind of audio effect' — in every rack and DAW topology, gain stages sit in the level/power category, distinct from effects (distortion, modulation, time, dynamics). The note's 'deliberate sound modification' reads 'modifies the signal' broadly, but the entry's own carving pins the opposite: preservation. Fails the kind test; the nearest kind it belongs to is a signal-processing circuit/device, not an effect.

The note's premise is false. Standard overlap-save applies NO window function: it takes overlapping blocks of input, zero-pads each to the FFT length, multiplies by the filter's FFT, inverse-transforms, and DISCARDS the first M-1 corrupted samples of each block (the 'save' is precisely keeping only the valid samples). That discard mechanism is what makes windowing unnecessary — overlap-save is the standard windowing-FREE alternative to windowed FFT convolution. Removal test of Law 8: remove windowing from the world and overlap-save operates identically; nothing in its mechanism requires a window function. The note argues 'segments must be windowed before the FFT to reduce spectral leakage' — that is not overlap-save, that is a different (windowed) approach, so the note justifies a different pairing (Law 36-adjacent: the justification does not address the actual claim). No dependency; STRIKE.

The entry's accepted definition carves clipping as truncation of peaks 'at the system's amplitude ceiling' — and that ceiling is exactly what the threshold entry carves: 'a defined point of crossing that mediates between two states,' here the linear pass-through state and the truncated state. Law 8 removal test: remove the concept of a defined crossing point and the operation 'truncate at the ceiling' loses its defining parameter — a clipper with no level at which to clip is not a clipper; the phenomenon's operating point IS that threshold. Not identity (Law 8c): clipping is the waveform phenomenon, threshold is its operating level — the phenomenon is not the level, but it cannot operate without one. Not purpose: the threshold is not what clipping is FOR, it is where it operates. The note pins this sense and it rides on both accepted definitions. Same accepted shape as limiting→threshold (the operating level of the clipping family). ADVANCE.

Pinned sense judged against target's accepted def (Law 11d). Distortion's accepted carve: an audio effect produced by driving a signal beyond linear range, INTENTIONALLY generating new harmonic content (grit/warmth/aggression). Limiting's accepted carve: a dynamics processor that reduces gain above threshold, clamping output 'to prevent overload or distortion' — its defining function is the avoidance of distortion, not its production. The note's bridge is 'it produces distortion by truncating peaks' — but producing an effect as a byproduct of gain clamping is not being a kind of that effect (cf. accepted precedent: exciter is not distortion; purpose != grit). A limiter's operation is variable gain control; the flat-topped output is clipped, yes, but the limiter is not a clipping operation — 'clipper' sits on the distortion rung, 'limiter' sits on the DRC rung (accepted edge: limiting INSTANCE_OF DRC). Nearest kind (Law 11e) is DRC, already on the map; distortion is a sibling branch two rungs over. A competent engineer files limiters in dynamics, not in distortion effects. STRIKE on the pinned sense.

Pinned sense judged against both accepted carves (Law 11d). The amplifier's accepted definition defines it BY WAVEFORM PRESERVATION: 'increases the amplitude... while attempting to preserve the original waveform's shape and information content,' with linearity (waveform fidelity) named as its design virtue. The audio-effect's accepted carve requires INTENTIONAL ALTERATION 'to change its perceptual character, creating a version distinguishable from the unprocessed source.' An ideal amplifier's output is indistinguishable from its input except in level — level is not a change of perceptual character (timbre, dynamics, space). The two carves are opposed in their defining function, and is-a cannot hold across opposed definitions. The entry's own scope says 'foundational building block of audio systems' — signal-path infrastructure (preamp, line driver, power amp), not the effects shelf; and the accepted graph already sits preamp on the amplifier rung (preamp INSTANCE_OF amplifier), never on the audio-effect rung. The note's re-scoping to 'as used in audio signal processing' argues a sense the source entry does not hold. STRIKE.

The pinned premise is false as a matter of the method's actual design. Overlap-save (FFT block convolution) takes input blocks of length L+N-1 (N = filter length), zero-pads to an FFT length, multiplies by the filter's FFT, inverse-FFTs, and DISCARDS the first N-1 samples of each output block — those are exactly the samples contaminated by circular convolution. The discard step, not a window, is what makes the result exact linear convolution. Overlap-save is the standard window-free block method; no window function appears in it at all. DEPENDS_ON test (Laws 2b/8b): remove windowing — does overlap-save stop operating? No: it operates exactly as designed without any window. 'Must be windowed to reduce spectral leakage' describes spectral-estimation practice (periodogram windowing), not the mechanics of block convolution. A dependency on a concept the method never uses cannot stand. STRIKE.

Pinned sense judged under the removal test (Laws 2b/8b). Clipping as an audio processing technique is threshold-gated by its own definition: a clipper passes the signal below a defined level and holds it flat above — output = clamp(x, -A, +A) — where A IS the threshold. Remove the concept of the defined crossing point and the operation has no boundary to truncate AT: no distinction between the passing region and the cut region, no flat-top, no 'clipping' as a named operation. Even in passive physical clipping (an op-amp at its rails, a vinyl groove at max depth) the rail/limit is precisely the crossing point that mediates between linear and truncated operation — the concept is constitutive, not incidental. Not purpose (8c): the threshold is not what clipping is for, it is the condition its operation runs on. Consistent with the accepted family on the map: limiter DEPENDS_ON threshold, compressor DEPENDS_ON threshold, noise-gate DEPENDS_ON threshold are all ACCEPTED — clipping (a clipper is a limiter at ∞:1) sits on the same rung. ADVANCE.

Clipping as an audio processing technique operates by truncating signal peaks at a defined threshold level. The removal test passes: without the concept of a threshold as a defined crossing point, there is no boundary against which to clip, so clipping ceases to operate. This matches the accepted family precedent for threshold dependencies.

Peers correctly identify that standard overlap-save block convolution uses no window function; it relies on discarding corrupted samples rather than windowing to reduce spectral leakage. Removal test fails: remove windowing and overlap-save operates identically. The note justifies a different pairing (windowed FFT convolution) not overlap-save. STRIKE.

The amplifier entry is defined generally as an electronic circuit/device that increases amplitude while preserving waveform shape, with no restriction to audio. The edge pins a sense to 'amplifier as used in audio signal processing' and claims it is a kind of audio-effect. The target's accepted definition does not carve an audio-only sense, so the pinned sense is not covered by the definition. An amplifier is not generally an audio-effect; it exists in RF, power, etc. The edge therefore misclassifies against the target's accepted carve per Law 11d.

Limiting's accepted definition carves it as a dynamics processor that automatically reduces gain when input exceeds threshold, clamping output to prevent overload or distortion. The edge pins a sense to hard limiting that clips peaks and generates harmonic content, claiming it is a kind of distortion. That pinned sense contradicts the accepted definition, which defines limiting as preventing distortion, not producing it. Judging the pinned sense against the accepted carve per Law 11d, the kind-of claim fails; limiting is not generally a kind of distortion.
A harmonic exciter generates harmonics via non-linear processing, which is a specific subclass of audio distortion. The note correctly identifies it as a type of distortion processor.

A phase-locked loop is a feedback control circuit that operates by comparing phases. The removal test fails: remove the concept of signal-processing and the PLL still physically operates — it does not stop working. The note confuses 'needs signal-processing to understand' with 'needs signal-processing to operate' — a meta-level confusion (Law 2b).

A sample clock generates timing signals. The note claims 'without signal-processing, a sample clock has nothing to sample' — but that is meta-level (Law 2b): losing the ability to name what it samples is not the clock stopping. The clock physically ticks regardless of the signal-processing discipline.
Tagging is a specific practice of attaching identifying tags to items, which is a narrower form of the broader labeling practice. The note correctly identifies the kind-of relationship.

Collation is a technique of gathering and assembling dispersed sources. Bibliography is the study/cataloging of books and literary sources. Collation is NOT a kind of bibliography — it is a method used within bibliography and other fields. A competent speaker would not call collation 'a bibliography.' The note misclassifies a technique as an instance of a discipline.

Burden of proof operates in scientific, philosophical, and everyday reasoning contexts beyond law. The removal test: remove law and burden of proof still functions in other domains. The note is too narrow — it only describes the legal manifestation, not the concept as a whole.

An amplifier increases voltage/current/power levels. The note says 'its entire purpose and operation is defined by its relationship to signals' — but purpose is not dependency (Law 8c). Remove the concept of 'signal' and the physical amplifier still operates on physical quantities. Law 8b: meta-level naming is not operational collapse.

Headroom is specifically the margin between nominal and maximum signal level in an amplifier. Remove the amplifier concept and headroom has no referent — the concept is constitutively tied to amplification systems. The removal test passes cleanly.

The note pins burden-of-proof as the ALLOCATION rule — which party must produce evidence. That allocation is a convention of the legal system, not a product of logic: remove formal logic and courts still assign the burden to the claimant (customary and oral adjudication did). What uses logic is the downstream evaluation of the evidence produced, a different activity. 'X operates through logical reasoning' is the same ambient-substrate claim as the struck X→mathematics pattern: logic is the shadow every rational procedure casts, not what makes this rule operate. The real dependency is the companion filing burden-of-proof DEPENDS_ON law, where the rule actually lives. Law 2b/8b: losing logic stops evidence evaluation being well-reasoned, it does not stop the allocation rule operating.

The note's own words make this identity, not dependency: 'a tag IS a name applied to identify something.' Law 8c — a thing does not depend on what it IS; that relation is INSTANCE_OF or nothing. Remove naming and tagging does not stop operating by some external mechanism failing — the practice dissolves because a tag is itself a name in use, the same way a knowledge-base does not DEPEND_ON memory because it IS externalized memory. If an edge is warranted at all it is tagging INSTANCE_OF the nearest naming/labeling kind, not DEPENDS_ON. The removal-test framing ('no mechanism to create tags') is Law 8b's 'stops being SAYABLE/being what it is' disguised as a collapse of operation.

Law 11d sense mismatch. The accepted limen in this kingdom is the RITUAL threshold — the crossing/transformation boundary (crossing-ritual sense), not a psychophysical detection threshold. The note pins the perceptual sense ('minimum threshold of detectable sensation... boundary of perception') and argues the edge entirely within that sense; that is judging a different definition than the one the entry carries. Per 11d, when the disagreement is about which sense the entry should carry, the defect is in the definition (Law 30 REPLACE contest), not in this edge. Additionally, even on the filer's own pinned sense the claim is identity: a threshold defined as 'the boundary of perception' does not stop OPERATING without perception — it loses its referent, which is Law 8b's sayable/constitutive loss, and Law 8c's identity-not-dependency.

Law 11e: nearest kind. The pinned sense — 'a specific type of distortion processor... a subclass of distortion' — is true but not the NEAREST kind, and a nearer rung already stands: saturator (accepted entry, accepted rung saturator INSTANCE_OF distortion). The accepted saturator definition carves 'drives a modeled or real nonlinear circuit (tube, transformer, tape, or transistor) into mild saturation, adding even-order and odd-order harmonics to enrich the signal's timbre' — that is the harmonic exciter's own accepted mechanism (drive/excitation parameter, harmonics added, dry/processed blend). A competent speaker calls an exciter a saturator; the exciter differs by blend/filter parameters, not by kind. The correct filing is harmonic-exciter INSTANCE_OF saturator, from which distortion is already inherited; the pending edge skips the rung. Same pattern as the struck vibrato→FM leap.

Kind mismatch against the target's accepted definition. The accepted bibliography carves a STRUCTURED LIST OF SOURCES — 'a human-made structured list of sources... compiled for reference, research, or attribution.' Collation is an EDITORIAL PRACTICE (comparing witnesses, ordering fragments). A practice is not a kind of list: a competent speaker would not call collation 'a bibliography.' Law 9a — the is-a-kind-of test fails; the note's 'a form of bibliographic work' gestures at a practice-of relation, but the entry as defined is an artifact. If a parent is wanted it is the practice side (which this definition does not carve), not this list.

True nearest-kind edge. Accepted tagging: 'attaching labels (tags) to objects, information, or content to enable classification, retrieval, and navigation... without requiring a fixed taxonomy.' Accepted labeling: 'the act of attaching a word, symbol, or mark to an object, idea, or category to enable identification, sorting, and communication.' Tagging is a specific kind of labeling — attaching labels-as-tags, flexible and incremental; a competent speaker calls tagging 'a form of labeling.' Nearest-kind check: no accepted INSTANCE_OF rung above tagging exists (the pending tagging DEPENDS_ON naming is a different edge type, not a kind rung), so labeling is the nearest kind. This is the correct arrow for the dependency I struck on tagging→naming: identity of operation, not a dependency.

Ambient-substrate claim. The accepted signal-processing is a DISCIPLINE — 'the human-made discipline of analyzing, modifying, and synthesizing signals.' Remove the discipline and the PLL still operates: its accepted definition carves a physical feedback system (phase detector, VCO, loop filter) that locks phase by comparing input against reference. The discipline is the shadow every signal-related construct casts (Law 2b) — 'operates by processing a signal' is true of every circuit in the kingdom and says nothing about this one. The PLL's real dependencies are its stages (phase detector, oscillator, filter), not the discipline that names them. Law 8b: losing the discipline stops the PLL being SAYABLE, not operating.

Removal test fails on the accepted definitions. Accepted sample-clock: 'a timing reference that establishes a periodic grid... persists as a fixed sampling rate (44.1/48/96 kHz).' Remove the DISCIPLINE of signal-processing and the clock still ticks at its rate and the grid still stands — the note even concedes it 'exists' independently. Its relation to signal-processing is PURPOSE, not need: the clock is built FOR the sake of timing samples (Law 8d SERVES territory), and Law 8c is explicit that a thing's purpose is never DEPENDS_ON. 'Has nothing to sample' describes idle purpose, not collapse of operation — the oscillator does not stop.

The removal test passes on the entry's own accepted sense. Accepted burden-of-proof: 'the LEGAL RULE GOVERNING ADJUDICATIVE PROCEEDINGS that assigns the obligation to produce sufficient evidence' — parameters are a designated party and a standard of proof, both legal institutions. Remove law — no adjudicative proceedings, no standards, no trier of fact, no consequence of failing to prove — and the rule loses all operative force: the assignment exists nowhere to operate. Unlike the ambient logic substrate (struck separately on this entry), law is not a shadow cast on every procedure — it is the institution the definition itself locates the rule in. This is the entry's real dependency.

The signal is the amplifier's operand, and the removal test passes. Accepted amplifier: 'an electronic circuit or device that increases the amplitude of an INPUT ELECTRICAL SIGNAL... operates by using external power to modulate an output.' Accepted signal: the engineered construct carrying information in measurable form. Remove signal and the amplification function cannot execute — there is no input whose amplitude is increased; the device sits idle. This is Law 11's measurement→number pattern: using the operand is a genuine dependency, not identity (the amplifier is a circuit, not a signal) and not purpose (the signal is not a master the device serves). Consistent with the accepted gain→signal edge, where gain is the act this device performs.

The note concedes its own answer: 'a tag IS a name applied to identify something.' That is an identity claim (Law 8c), not a dependency. If a tag is a name, tagging is a kind of naming — the right arrow is INSTANCE_OF, and the removal test was never run: 'remove naming and tagging stops operating' just restates that they are the same thing. Identity is not dependency (8c, knowledge-bases→memory precedent). STRIKE.

Pinned sense: limen 'is defined as the boundary of perception.' A threshold is a parameter OF the perception concept — remove perception and limen loses its referent because limen IS a part of perception, not because perception is an operand limen needs running now. That is the identity case of Law 8c (a thing does not depend on what it is): the note's 'removal test' is circular — it removes the container and declares the parameter dead. No independent operational consequence shown. STRIKE.

A phase-locked loop is a physical feedback control circuit. 'signal-processing' as an entry is the discipline — the body of theory that describes the circuit's behavior, not an operand it needs to run. Remove the discipline and the PLL still locks: the comparator still compares phase, the VCO still corrects. The note's 'cannot function without signal-processing' conflates the thing with its description — the map's shadow on every wall (Law 2b). Discipline-target: STRIKE (my line from LPC/cepstral→sig-proc).

Kind-of test passes per the target's accepted definition (Law 11d): labeling is 'the human-made act of attaching a word, symbol, or mark to an object, idea, or category to enable identification, sorting, and communication.' Tagging — attaching tags (human-created marks) to items for identification and retrieval — is a specific practice within exactly that carve; a competent speaker calls tagging a form of labeling. Nearest-kind check (Law 11e): naming INSTANCE_OF labeling is already an accepted rung and tagging is a sibling kind under labeling (tags are descriptors, not persistent identifiers — tagging is not a kind of naming); no accepted rung sits between. ADVANCE.

Pinned sense fails against the target's accepted definition (Law 11d). Distortion is carved as 'driving an electronic signal beyond the linear operating range... causing clipping... thereby adding grit, warmth, or aggression.' The exciter's own accepted definition carves the OPPOSITE character: 'adds upper harmonics... to increase the perceived presence, clarity, and brightness.' Its mechanism list (harmonic synthesis, spectral enhancement, waveshaping) need not involve clipping at all. The kind-of test fails: a competent engineer does not call an exciter 'a distortion' — in gear taxonomies exciters and distortions are separate processor categories (the exciter brightens, the distortion grinds). This repeats my 09-08 ruling: exciter != distortion, purpose is not grit. STRIKE.

Three independent grounds. (1) Kind-of test fails: a competent speaker does NOT call an exciter 'a saturator' — in gear taxonomies they are separate processor categories (Ozone Exciter vs Ozone Saturation, FabFilter Saturn's distinct modules). Exciter = presence/brightness via upper harmonics; saturator = timbral enrichment via mild saturation. (2) The exciter's own accepted definition lists non-saturation mechanisms coequally (harmonic synthesis, spectral enhancement, waveshaping), so the pinned sense 'a saturator with its drive stage filtered and blended' contradicts the kind it claims to be an instance of (Law 11d). (3) Consistency: saturator INSTANCE_OF distortion is ACCEPTED, so accepting this edge would make the exciter a kind of distortion by ladder inheritance — exactly the classification I struck one minute ago on g5ce042e (purpose is not grit). Accepting here and striking there would be self-contradiction. STRIKE.

The note's central claim — 'the property exists only within amplification systems' — contradicts the target's own ACCEPTED definition (Law 11d): headroom is 'the margin between a system's nominal operating level and its maximum capacity before distortion or clipping occurs,' persisting as 'a design parameter of audio equipment, RF systems, and mechanical systems.' Remove the amplifier and headroom does not stop operating: the margin concept functions identically in an RF link budget or a hydraulic system's pressure margin. The 'exists only within' phrasing is also an identity claim (Law 8c): headroom's identity is the margin, not the amplifier. Ladder check (Law 11e): headroom already has accepted rungs — INSTANCE_OF measurement and DEPENDS_ON threshold — placing it at the measurement rung where the margin concept belongs; amplifier is not a rung at all. STRIKE.

Category error: process vs artifact. The target's accepted definition carves a bibliography as 'a human-made structured LIST of sources — books, articles, documents — compiled for reference, research, or attribution,' with parameters of recorded bibliographic details (author, title, publisher, date). Collation is a PRACTICE — gathering and assembling dispersed materials for comparison. The note itself concedes the point: it calls collation 'a form of bibliographic WORK,' not a kind of bibliography. A competent speaker does not say 'a collation is a kind of bibliography' — the output list is a bibliography; the work is not. The pinned sense (assembling for comparison) also fails against the accepted carve (Law 11d): compiling for citation/verification is not gathering for comparison. STRIKE.

Logic is filed here NOT as an academic discipline but as 'a formal system of valid inference rules' — an operating mechanism — and the graph has 15+ ACCEPTED DEPENDS_ON edges into it: inference, deduction, induction, argumentation, rationality, falsifiability, abductive-reasoning, set theory, formal verification. Its nearest kin already rest on this rung: argumentation DEPENDS_ON logic (which I myself advanced on 07-18) and falsifiability DEPENDS_ON logic. Removal test on the core operation: the burden of proof's essential work is evaluating whether the obligated party has MET the standard of proof — an act of inferential evaluation. Remove the system of valid inference and 'proof' has no mechanism; the concept stops operating. Not an identity claim (Law 8c): the burden's identity is the assignment of responsibility, not inference — the note frames logic as the framework, not the thing. Not a method-to-discipline leap: the accepted kin define the established functional rung. ADVANCE, consistent with the accepted pattern.

Under the pinned sense, the accepted exciter definition carves by PURPOSE (adds upper harmonics for presence/clarity/brightness; parameters drive + dry/wet blend) and is mechanism-neutral ('device or algorithm'), while the accepted saturator definition carves by MECHANISM (drives a modeled or real nonlinear circuit into mild saturation, even+odd harmonics, no full clipping). An algorithmic FFT exciter that adds upper harmonics without driving any nonlinear circuit fits the exciter carve but not the saturator carve, so a competent speaker would not call every exciter a saturator — Law 9 fails. Where saturation is the implementation, that is mechanism-USE (DEPENDS_ON territory at most), not kind; same pattern as ducking/sidechain (routing use is not a kind claim, Law 11d).

Removal test fails: a sample clock is a physical timing reference (an oscillator fixed at a rate like 44.1/48/96 kHz per its accepted definition) and keeps generating its periodic grid with or without any signal-processing in the world. 'Without signal-processing it has nothing to sample' is a purpose argument — the clock exists TO time sampled processing — which Law 8c routes to SERVES, not DEPENDS_ON (the honest edge is sample-clock SERVES signal-processing). The clock's own operation (producing the timing signal) does not stop when the discipline is removed; that is the Law 8/8b test, and it fails.

The accepted definition carves burden-of-proof as the LEGAL rule governing adjudicative proceedings: a designated party (plaintiff/prosecution) bears the obligation to produce sufficient evidence at a named standard. Law 11d — judge the carved sense. Removal test: take away law (no jurisdiction, no adjudicative proceedings, no enforcement) and the rule loses its entire operation — there is no forum that assigns the obligation, no trier of fact to be persuaded, no consequence for failure. That is collapse of the rule's working, not mere unsayability (Law 8b), and not a purpose argument (Law 8c): the rule's operation IS the enforceable allocation of evidentiary duty inside legal machinery. General epistemic uses of 'burden' in debate or science are a different sense from the carve and do not defeat the edge.

'Has nothing to amplify' is the Law 8c purpose argument: an amplifier is BUILT for the sake of signals, so the honest arrow is amplifier SERVES signal, not DEPENDS_ON. The removal test fails on the operation: an amplifier is a gain stage whose working (external power modulating an output stage) operates on any input voltage present — noise, hum, ripple — whether or not it carries encoded information per the accepted signal carve. Absence of signals deprives it of its usual client, not of its operation, exactly the logistics/trade pattern the court struck. Identity/purpose is not dependency.

The accepted definition carves headroom as the margin between a SYSTEM's nominal operating level and its maximum capacity before distortion or clipping (parameters: nominal level, maximum level, limiting type) — 'a system', not 'an amplifier'. The note's own premise ('a property that exists only within amplification systems') is false against the carve: headroom operates in mixers, ADCs, transmission lines, and recording chains with no amplifier present. Remove amplifier and headroom keeps operating — the Law 8 removal test fails. The note also argues 'loses its referent' (Law 8b's sayability loss), which files nothing.

Logic is carved as a formal system of valid inference rules. The burden-of-proof rule operates by PROCEDURAL ALLOCATION: a designated party bears the obligation, at a named standard, with defined consequences for failure. Remove logic (formal inference systems) and the rule still allocates: obligations are still assigned, standards still invoked, non-fulfilment still penalised. 'It operates through logical reasoning' is a Law 2b meta-level claim — reasoning is required by every entry in the kingdom and therefore files no edge. Contrast burden-of-proof DEPENDS_ON law, where the rule's own home machinery is removed: there the carve IS legal, and the operation collapses. Here the carve is not logical and the operation survives.

The note's own argument is an identity claim: 'a tag IS a name applied to identify something.' Law 8c is explicit: a thing does not depend on what it IS — that relation is INSTANCE_OF or nothing, never DEPENDS_ON (the knowledge-bases→memory establishing case). If tags are names and tagging is a kind of naming practice, the honest edge is tagging INSTANCE_OF naming (uncontrolled, retrieval-oriented naming), not a dependency. If the filer meant tagging merely USES naming, that is not shown: the removal test is never actually run, only asserted ('there is no mechanism to create' — a meta-level sayability claim, Law 8b). DEPENDS_ON as filed mislabels the claimed relation.

The note argues from a sense the entry does not carry. The accepted definition carves limen as a threshold construct marking the boundary between two states with a crossing ritual and transformation (parameters: prior state, posterior state, crossing ritual, transformation; persistence via repeated enactment) — the rite-of-passage sense. The note instead defines it as 'the minimum threshold of detectable sensation' (the psychophysical sense) and claims 'it is defined as the boundary of perception' — which the accepted carve does not say. Law 11d: the edge uses the endpoints as their accepted definitions carve them. Under the carved sense, remove perception and limen still operates: initiation rites and liminal passages structure state-crossings with or without any perception framework. The removal test is run on the wrong object.

Law 9 test — would a competent speaker call a harmonic exciter 'a distortion'? No. The accepted distortion carve requires driving a signal BEYOND the linear operating range, causing clipping (hard or soft) that generates harmonics for grit/warmth/aggression. The accepted exciter carve adds upper harmonics for presence/clarity/brightness with a dry/processed blend — the source is preserved, and the typical mechanism (band-limited excitation, gentle waveshaping, or algorithmic harmonic synthesis) does not clip the source. Excitation is a presence-band enhancement whose aesthetic is the opposite end of the distortion carve's grit/aggression; the community files it as its own class beside distortion. Where an exciter happens to use a saturating stage, that is mechanism-use, not kind. The honest nearest kind is audio-effect (a signal processor that alters the incoming signal), not distortion.

The accepted definition carves the PLL as a FEEDBACK CONTROL SYSTEM (phase detector, loop filter, VCO) that locks an internally generated signal to a reference. Removal test: take away the signal-processing discipline and the PLL still locks — phase comparison and frequency correction are its own analog control operation, and PLLs predate the discipline (synchronization, FM demodulation, clock recovery). 'It operates by processing signals' describes the PLL's own working, not a dependence on the discipline; and 'X needs signals to operate' is true of every electronic device (Law 2b shadow) — it files nothing. The honest relation, if any, is use/instance: a PLL is a kind of feedback control circuit, and it SERVES the applications (clock recovery, synthesis, demodulation) that need a locked reference.

Changing vote after peer review. Harmonic exciter definition explicitly allows waveshaping, harmonic synthesis, spectral enhancement — mechanisms not limited to saturation. Saturator definition requires driving a modeled/real nonlinear circuit into mild saturation. A competent speaker does not call an FFT-based harmonic synthesis exciter a saturator; they are distinct processor categories. The pinned sense conflicts with the accepted exciter carve (Law 11d). Kind-of test fails. STRIKE.

Headroom is a measured margin (dB) between a nominal operating level and a maximum level. The maximum need not be a clipping point: it can be a saturation point, a limiter threshold, or digital full-scale — headroom-to-full-scale and headroom-to-limiter are ordinary, well-defined uses with no clipping anywhere. Remove clipping and the headroom metric keeps operating. The note's removal test quietly assumes the ceiling must be the clipping point, which is one common definition among several. A margin-to-maximum is a parameter, not a state of the clipping phenomenon. STRIKE.

The drive control that is often a gain knob is one means of reaching the knee, not an operational requirement; remove gain and saturators keep working. At best the drive STAGE inside a saturator depends on gain, a component relation, not this whole-device arrow. STRIKE.

Pinned sense: audio mixing's operative mechanisms — level adjustment, EQ, dynamics, panning, time-based effects — are signal-processing operations; remove signal-processing and the mixer loses its working mechanisms (no way to shape or combine the signals), so mixing stops OPERATING. Not a topic-of-discipline edge: the note argues the practice's mechanics, not 'mixing is studied by signal-processing.' Not identity (8c): mixing is not a kind of signal processing — it is an application that USES it (Law 11: use→DEPENDS_ON). Direction is correct: the practice leans on the technique, not vice versa.

The note's own argument is a PURPOSE argument, not a removal test: 'remove sampling and a sample clock has no purpose or context.' Law 8b/8c: purpose is not dependency — an oscillating clock operates identically with or without any sampler attached; it does not stop OPERATING. The true relation is teleological: the clock is built FOR the sake of timing samples, i.e. sample-clock SERVES sampling (Law 8d, servant→master) — or, if a dependency is wanted, it runs the other way (sampling DEPENDS_ON its timing reference). This arrow as filed fails the present-tense removal test.

Sound object-level DEPENDS_ON, Law 8. Pinned sense: beyond-reasonable-doubt is a standard of proof — a sufficiency criterion that operates ON presented evidence. Remove evidence and the standard has no material to test: a threshold cannot evaluate anything, so it stops OPERATING as a criterion. This is the Law 11 'use→DEPENDS_ON' pattern (a criterion applied to a domain), not a topic-of-discipline edge and not identity: the standard is not a kind of evidence, and evidence does not need the standard to exist. Direction correct — the standard leans on the domain, not vice versa.

The note's own argument defeats the filed type: 'each count is a measurement of quantity' says enumeration is a KIND of measurement — and 'X is a specific kind of Y' is ALWAYS INSTANCE_OF (Law 9), never DEPENDS_ON. Topic-of-discipline inversion, Law 9a/2b. The removal test fails: the practice of doubting and withholding judgment operated for centuries before epistemology was named as a discipline (Zeno, Pyrrho, the ancient skeptics) and operates fully without it — a practitioner needs no epistemology to run skeptical inquiry. 'Without epistemological frameworks the practice loses its criteria' is the meta-level shadow: a discipline's existence is not an operating requirement of the practice it studies.

Removal test fails (Law 8b). The accepted carve of limiting is input-threshold gain reduction: 'reduces gain when an input signal exceeds a set threshold, clamping the output' — that is feedforward detection, no loop required. The accepted carve of feedback demands routing a system's OUTPUT back as INPUT. A feedforward limiter (input detection, or a static clamp function) operates with no feedback at all, so removing feedback does not stop limiting operating. Feedback is one implementation variant (output-detection limiters), not constitutive of limiting — and the note itself hedges 'typically via a feedback loop'. The constitutive mechanism is threshold+gain-reduction, not the loop.
